question: What is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder?

title: CONTENT
question: Who is generally eligible to apply for an OCI card?
answer: Most foreign nationals of full age and capacity are eligible if they meet one of the following criteria: • They were an Indian citizen on or after January 26, 1950. • They were eligible to become an Indian citizen on January 26, 1950. • They belonged to a territory that became part of India after August 15, 1947. • They are a child, grandchild, or great-grandchild of someone who meets the above criteria.

title: CONTENT
question: Can minor children apply for an OCI card?
answer: Yes. A minor child is eligible if: • They are the child of a person eligible for an OCI card. • Both of their parents are citizens of India, or at least one parent is a citizen of India.

question: I am the spouse of an Indian citizen. Am I eligible?

question: What is the role of the FRRO in India?
answer: The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) operates under the Bureau of Immigration (Ministry of Home Affairs). It manages immigration functions and handles all registration and visa-related services for foreign nationals within its specific jurisdiction.

title: FOREIGNER REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS (FRRO/FRO)
answer: Foreign nationals must register with the Foreigner’s Regional Registration Office (FRRO) or the Foreigner’s Registration Office (FRO) based on their visa category, stay duration, and specific endorsements on their visa.

title: FOREIGNER REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS (FRRO/FRO)
question: Who are required to register within 14 days of arrival?
answer: Foreigners entering India on the following visa types must register within 14 days if their visa is valid for more than 180 days: • Student Visa • Employment Visa • Medical Visa • Missionary Visa

title: FOREIGNER REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS (FRRO/FRO)
question: When does a Business Visa holder need to register?
answer: A Business Visa holder is required to register if: • Their continuous stay in India exceeds 180 days.

title: CONTENT
question: Are there registration requirements for other visa types?
answer: Yes. Foreigners on any visa type (excluding those on Official or Diplomatic passports) must register if their continuous stay on a single entry or their aggregate stay in a calendar year exceeds 180 days.

title: CONTENT
question: What are the specific registration rules for Pakistani nationals?
answer: Pakistani nationals face stricter timelines and must register with the local FRO within 24 hours of their arrival in India.

title: CONTENT
question: Which categories of people are exempt from registration?
answer: The following groups do not need to register with the FRRO/FRO: • Children: Anyone below 12 years of age. • OCI Cardholders: Overseas Citizens of India are fully exempt. • Neighbouring Citizens: Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan do not require a visa or registration.

title: CONTENT
question: What happens if a foreigner fails to register?
answer: Non-compliance with registration rules is a serious matter and shall result in legal consequences, which may include fines, restrictions on future travel, or deportation.

title: CONTENT

answer: Yes. All foreigners must strictly adhere to any specific conditions or stipulations endorsed on their visa at all times. SPECIAL CATEGORY REGISTRATION (Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh)

title: REPORTING THE DEATH OF A FOREIGN NATIONAL
question: Is it mandatory to report the death of a foreigner in India?
answer: Yes. It is mandatory to report the death of any foreign national to the jurisdictional FRRO (Foreigners Regional Registration Office) or FRO.

title: REPORTING THE DEATH OF A FOREIGN NATIONAL
question: Do hospitals have a responsibility to report the death?
answer: Yes. Every hospital, nursing home, or medical institution must report the death of a foreigner occurring on their premises within seven days. This notification must be sent electronically via email to the jurisdictional FRRO/FRO.

title: TRANSPORTING MORTAL REMAINS ABROAD
question: What is required to transport a deceased foreigner back to their native country?
answer: A relative or authorized representative must apply for a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the jurisdictional FRRO/FRO.

question: What documents are needed for an NOC for international transportation?
answer: You will need to provide: • Official Certificates: Death Certificate (Municipality/Panchayat) and a Death Report from the local Police Station. • Travel Documents: Copy of the deceased’s Passport and Visa, plus the Passport/Visa of the carrier and a copy of the flight ticket. • Medical Records: Death summary from the Hospital and an Embalming Certificate from an authorized institution. • Authorization: A request letter from the family to the FRRO and a formal letter from the relevant Embassy or Consulate.

title: CONTENT
question: Can a foreign national be cremated or buried in India?
answer: Yes, but an NOC for Cremation/Burial must be obtained from the jurisdictional FRRO/FRO first.

title: CONTENT
question: What documents are required for local cremation or burial?
answer: The requirements include: • Official Records: Death Certificate, Police Death Report, and Hospital Death Summary. • Deceased's Info: Copy of the passport and visa. • Permission/Proofs: NOC from the Church, Mosque, or Crematorium; Indian Address Proof; and a Marriage Certificate (if the deceased was married to an Indian citizen). • Family Requests: A letter from the family to the FRRO, a request letter from the relative along with their passport copy, and a letter from the Embassy or Consulate.

title: MEDICAL TREATMENT & VISA RULES
question: Can a foreigner receive medical treatment on a primary visa (like a Tourist or Business visa)?
answer: Yes. Any foreigner, including Pakistani nationals, suffering from a minor medical condition that only requires OPD (Outpatient Department) consultation, can receive treatment at any hospital using their existing primary visa.

title: MEDICAL TREATMENT & VISA RULES
question: What happens if a Pakistani national requires hospitalization?
answer: If a Pakistani national needs to avail of indoor medical treatment (admission to a hospital), they are required to convert their primary visa into a Medical Visa.

title: MEDICAL TREATMENT & VISA RULES
question: When must other foreign nationals (non-Pakistani) convert to a Medical Visa?
answer: A foreigner should apply to convert their primary visa to a Medical Visa in either of the following two scenarios: 1. Extended Stay: The medical treatment is expected to exceed the stay duration allowed by the primary visa. 2. Organ Transplant: The treatment for the disease specifically requires an organ transplant.

title: MEDICAL TREATMENT & VISA RULES
question: How does a foreigner apply for this visa conversion?
answer: The application should be submitted through the official e-FRRO portal (indianfrro.gov.in). All visa conversions are subject to the specific terms and conditions laid down by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). It is best to apply as soon as the medical necessity is identified to avoid overstaying the original visa.

question: Can a former Indian national continue to use their Indian passport after getting a foreign one?
answer: There is a strict 3-month grace period starting from the day of acquisition of the new nationality (e.g., the date on the Naturalization Certificate). Once that grace period expires, holding, acquiring, or traveling on an Indian passport constitutes an offense under the Indian Passport Act, 1967, and attracts severe penalties.

question: What must a person do if they acquire foreign citizenship while they are staying in India?
answer: If an individual acquires foreign nationality while residing in India, they must take the following steps: • Obtain the passport of their new nationality. • Surrender their Indian passport, Indian Voter ID, Indian Ration card, and all other relevant Indian nationality documents. • Apply for appropriate visa services on the e-FRRO portal (https://indianfrro.gov.in) within 30 days of acquiring the foreign nationality.

title: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR FORM III
question: What is Form III and who needs to fill it?
answer: Form III is a mandatory report that every "keeper of accommodation" must submit when a foreign national (including OCI cardholders) stays at their premises. This includes hotels, homestays, hospitals, and even religious institutions.

title: CONTENT

title: CONTENT
question: In what language should the records be maintained in accommodation?
answer: Records should ideally be in English if the host is able to understand. If not, an Indian language is acceptable. If the guest doesn't understand the requirements, it is the host's duty to explain the rules to them.

title: CONTENT
question: How long must these records be kept in accommodation?
answer: The keeper of the accommodation must maintain electronic records of these particulars for at least one year. These must be available for inspection at any time by a Registration Officer, District Magistrate, or a Police Officer (Head Constable rank or above).

title: CONTENT
question: What is the deadline for submitting the arrival report by keeper of the accommodation?
answer: The arrival details must be transmitted electronically through the official portal or mobile app within 24 hours of the foreigner’s arrival.

title: CONTENT
question: Does the keeper of the accommodation need to report when the guest leaves?
answer: Yes. Departure details, including the date, time, and the address to which the guest is proceeding, must also be submitted within 24 hours of their departure.

title: CONTENT
question: I run a small homestay; do I really need to do form III entry?
answer: Yes. The definition of "accommodation" is very broad. It includes: • Hotels, hostels, boarding houses, and sarais. • Private rentals, homestays, and paying guest (PG) houses. • Clubs, dak-bungalows, rest houses, and tents. • Hospitals and nursing homes.

title: PENALTIES AND LEGAL CONSEQUENCES
question: What actions constitute a violation under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025?
answer: Legal or penal action may be taken against a foreigner for the following violations: • Overstaying beyond the visa validity or stay stipulation. • Non-registration with the FRRO/FRO when required. • Engaging in unauthorized activities that do not match the specific visa category granted (e.g., working on a tourist visa). • Non-filing of requisite forms (such as Form III for accommodations). • Any other contravention of provisions or orders made under the Act.

question: What is an ETA?
answer: ETA is an Electronic Travel Authorization. It allows the bearer access into the issuing country (India). ETA is NOT eVisa. When the bearer of ETA is allowed entry into India by the Immigration Officer, it becomes eVisa. eVisa will be stamped on the Passport of the foreigner at the designated ICPs on production of valid ETA.

question: What is the difference between “ETA Expiry date” and “Visa Expiry Date”?
answer: ETA expiry date is the last date allowing bearer access into India. Visa Expiry Date is the last date permitted for the stay of foreigner in India subjected to any stay stipulation applicable.

question: What is the difference between “Visa validity/Visa expiry date” and “Stay stipulation”?
answer: Visa validity or Visa expiry date refers to the validity period during which the foreigner can stay in India on the strength of Visa subject to stay stipulations. Stay stipulations are the rules which determine the number of days a foreigner may be permitted to stay in India on the strength of Visa. Stay stipulations are of two kinds 1) Continuous stay in India from the date of last arrival. 2) Total Aggregate stay in India during the calendar year.

answer: Calendar year refers to period from 1st January to 31st December of the current year.

title: CONTENT
question: What is “total aggregate stay in a calendar year” and “continuous stay”?
answer: Total Aggregate stay refers to total period of stay of foreigner in India including multiple visits during the calendar year. Continuous stay refers to period of stay of foreigner in India since his last arrival.
